method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: Size-of-sets driver and introduction OLP-0027-0028 plus all 31 translated content blocks of OLP-0029.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An informal enumeration is a beginning-indexed finite-or-infinite list on which every set element occurs at a finite position; order and repetitions may vary, and the empty list enumerates the empty set.
samples.checks: Finite position, beginning, repetitions, order and the empty-set convention are all explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For a nonempty set, a formal enumeration is a surjection from the positive integers. A finite list is extended by repeating its last element; this construction fails only for the empty list.
samples.checks: Nonempty qualification and last-element construction retained; surjective is not weakened to merely functional.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Enumerable means empty or possessing an enumeration, so finite and empty sets count as enumerable even though the Marathi witness emphasizes countably infinite sets.
samples.checks: OpenLogic convention controls the definition; no computability requirement imported.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The integer enumeration alternates zero, positive and negative values; the piecewise cases and ceiling formula are preserved exactly.
samples.checks: Reader note identifies the source table's missing f(7) value without altering the formula or table cells.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Finite unions and subsets of enumerable sets are enumerable, with empty-set cases handled separately where a surjection from positive integers cannot exist.
samples.checks: All exercise prompts retain their construction requirements and boundary-case questions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Surjections from positive integers and from natural numbers are equivalent by shifting the argument by one.
samples.checks: Both directions and their unchanged n+1 and n-1 formulas remain in the right order.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Removing repetitions recursively yields a bijection from either the positive integers or a finite initial segment; injectivity and surjectivity are proved separately.
samples.checks: Finite versus infinite domains, recursive first-unused-value construction and both function properties retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The final exercise asks for equivalence between an injection into the positive integers and either emptiness or a surjection from the positive integers.
samples.checks: Directions, empty alternative and function orientations preserved.

limitations: T060-T063 are provisional and explicitly open to correction.
